item.description:

item.title: Elementary Educator Ceramics Workshop — Tue Jul 28, 5:30 PM — Davis Arts Center
item.description:
If you’re an elementary school teacher and have been wanting to introduce clay projects in your classroom, this three-day workshop is for you! Build your understanding of ceramics and gain the confidence to lead engaging clay projects with your students. In a supportive environment, you’ll learn kid-friendly projects that can be completed in a single day or over multiple weeks, and you’ll receive hands-on guidance in loading and firing a kiln. Connect with a creative community of fellow elementary school teachers and leave with practical skills and project ideas you can bring directly into your classroom! ● Day 1: One-day and weekly projects ● Day 2: Underglazing, textures & loading a bisque kiln ● Day 3: Glazing & loading a glaze kiln Instructor: Vex Rios (They/Them/Theirs) AGES 18+ Price: $150 Time: Tuesdays, 5:30-8:00 pm Workshop date: July 14-July 28

item.title: Adrian West Band Live — Sat Jul 25, 8:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description: Adrian West Band is a rising force in the Bay Area music scene. Based in Oakland, the six-piece band plays original acoustic rock which they dub “Paul Simon meets Talking Heads”. A classically trained violinist who later turned to drums, guitar and singing, Adrian is a gifted composer and arranger. His lyrics, which range from whimsical to philosophical, ride atop a steady wave of catchy music. He always writes the music first and lyrics second, only adding lyrics if he feels the music stands tall on its own. Fun fact: Paul Simon and David Byrne (of Talking Heads) work pretty much the same way. Adrian figured out a while ago that he likes having trained jazz musicians in his band. Jazz musicians bring technical chops and versatility. They know how to listen to each other and make a song flourish. item.title: Surface Tension by Roma Devanbu — Sun Jul 26, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: ROMA DEVANBU SURFACE TENSION July 3 – August 2, 2026 Second Saturday Reception July 11th, 5-8 PM Roma Devanbu has been making and exhibiting her paintings and mix-media work for decades. In Surface Tension, her first exhibit exclusively of photographs, we see her hungry painters eye hunting and gathering brush marks, patterns and textures in the wide world around her. Devanbu says “Inside the studio I manipulate materials. I rub, tear, fold, cut, glue and paint to create images on paper and canvas. When I leave the studio my creative actions gain a broader context and I understand my gestures as echoes of larger elemental forces acting on natural and man-made surfaces.” The photographs in this exhibition are records of a physical world in which materials collide, collaborate, stretch, erode, rust, scratch, drape, freeze and embrace. The subjects are approached in an unapologetically straight forward manner, presenting the plain facts within the scope of her viewfinder. But, each t

item.title: Who are Orientals: Magenta Realism — Sun Jul 26, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SHARON TSAO WHO ARE ORIENTALS: MAGENTA REALISM July 3 – August 2, 2026 Second Saturday Reception: July 11, 5–8 PM About forty years ago, when I first came to California, I was told that I was “Oriental.” I was also told that certain tables and chests were “Oriental,” and that a particular decorative style was likewise considered “Oriental,” even though these things looked unfamiliar to me. The works in this exhibition are largely produced in what I was told is an “Oriental” style or manner. They originate from dried Boston ivy vines resembling twisted tree branches, gathered after years of growth without human intervention and coated with an artificial magenta surface. The application of magenta coating violently interrupts this natural index. Historically, magenta is among the first fully synthetic modern pigments, inseparable from industrial chemistry, mechanical reproduction, and the chromatic excess of modernity. item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Oct 22, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Oct 22, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.description:
The beloved Picnic in the Park season is back at the Davis Farmers Market starting Wednesday, April 1, 2026! Every Wednesday evening through August 26, the market expands to 4:00 – 8:00 PM, turning Central Park into the perfect spot for a relaxed picnic dinner. Shop fresh produce, artisan goods, and a wide variety of prepared foods from your favorite vendors. Enjoy local craft beer, wine, and brand new this year – mead! Each week features live music and children’s activities, creating a festive, family-friendly atmosphere. Bring blankets, lawn chairs, and reusable bags. It’s the ideal way to unwind, connect with neighbors, and support local farmers and food makers. This year is extra special as the Davis Farmers Market celebrates its 50th Anniversary!
